title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
layout_note: Three tables left to right: a 4-row logical KV-block grid, a small block table in the middle, and a tall 9-row physical KV-block grid on the right; arrows run from logical rows through the block table to scattered physical rows. A request circle with its prompt and outputs sits top-left.
grouping: Each table has a bold title above it, with the words Logical and Physical in red; there are no enclosing frames. Rows are labelled Block 0, Block 1, ... at the left of both grids, so the reader can match logical and physical blocks by label.
shapes_depth: Flat. Grids of square-cornered cells with thin black lines; filled cells are pale yellow holding italic words, cells written during decoding are a darker yellow-orange. The block table has a grey header row. Small circled numerals mark the order of steps on cells and on the thin black arrows.
proposed_highlight: The red words Logical and Physical contrast the two address spaces, and the darker yellow-orange cells mark the tokens added while generating, which appear at the same position in both grids.
lesson: Show an indirection (virtual-to-physical mapping) as two grids of the same row height on either side of a small lookup table, writing the same real words into matching cells so the reader can check the mapping by content.
notes: elements 'arrow-labels' = circled step numerals on arrows and cells. Figure 4 is the system overview (scheduler, KV cache manager, workers); Figure 6 was chosen because it draws the PagedAttention mechanism itself. Venue from the first page (SOSP '23 footer).

arrangement.units: three unframed tables side by side, each titled above: logical blocks grid, block table, physical blocks grid
arrangement.inputs_as: a circle labelled 'Request A' with the quoted prompt and output words beside it, at the top left
arrangement.shared: the block table in the middle is the only link between the grids; arrows enter it from logical rows and fan out from it to physical rows

taxonomy.task: KV-cache memory management for LLM serving

core.what: a logical KV-block grid on the left and a taller physical KV-block grid on the right flank a small block table, and arrows through the table land on non-adjacent physical rows filled with the same words

relations.form: both grids are tables of 4-slot blocks filled with the real prompt words ('Four score and seven', 'years ago our fathers', 'brought'), one word per cell
arrows run from each logical block row into the block table and out to its physical block (logical 0 -> physical 7, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 3), so the scattered placement is seen by where the arrows land
small circled step numbers on cells, table entries and arrows mark the order of allocation, and '# filled' entries show updates like 3 -> 4
the request is a circle 'Request A' at top left with its quoted prompt and outputs, whose words reappear in the grids below

channels.colour: pale yellow = filled KV slot from the prompt, darker yellow-orange = newly generated token; red title words separate 'Logical' from 'Physical'
channels.shape: grid of cells = KV blocks, small two-column table = block table, circle = request
channels.line: thin black arrows = address mapping through the block table
channels.frame: none; the three tables stand unframed side by side, titled above

quality.strengths: The method is drawn on its own data structure: the same words can be found in contiguous logical blocks and in scattered physical blocks, so non-contiguous paging is visible as geometry; the block table sits exactly between the two address spaces it maps; newly generated tokens are distinguished by one tint.
quality.weaknesses: The mapping arrows from the table to physical blocks 1, 3 and 7 are long diagonals that cross each other; circled step numbers are tiny and repeated on cells, table and arrows, making the order hard to read at print size; red is used only on two title words.

insights.structure: A short logical grid on the left and a tall physical grid on the right flank a small block table, and arrows through the table land on non-adjacent physical rows.
insights.data: Real prompt words (italic) fill the KV cells, one word per cell, so the same words can be found again in the scattered physical blocks.
insights.emphasis: Red 'Logical' and 'Physical' title words and darker yellow-orange cells for newly generated tokens make the two address spaces and the growth step stand out.
insights.flow: Start at the request top-left, read the logical grid, pass through the block table, then follow the arrows right to the physical rows; circled numerals give step order.
insights.avoid: The long thin arrows from the block table cross each other on the way to the physical grid, and the circled numerals on them are too small to read at print size.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
